title: Learned community models prioritize a tested bacterial colonization inhibitor
summary: Models trained on community composition helped identify Enterococcus faecalis as an inhibitor of Enterococcus faecium colonization in human stool-derived laboratory communities. Follow-up supported the predicted interaction under the tested conditions. The result was public in an April 2023 preprint before the March 2024 journal article. It does not demonstrate prevention of infection or beneficial intervention in humans.
organization: Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Brigham and Women's Hospital; Harvard Medical School

evidence.unknown: Host effects, clinical benefit and transfer beyond the culture conditions remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest and neural-ODE community models supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv API v1 abstract/date; journal article selected model and intervention Results, metadata and affiliations. Detailed final-version counts not transferred.
